contracts.legacy_behavior: One Rust database owner and writer publish typed pure queries asynchronously.
contracts.target_behavior: The durable topology keeps the RFC 011 ownership and query laws unchanged.
contracts.migration: No semantic migration; retain the architecture ownership ratchet.
contracts.rollback: Existing RFC 011 owner and query paths remain the rollback authority.

evidence.claim: The shipped runtime graph rejects a second database/query authority.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Notifications are hints; generations and per-object source order govern reconciliation.
contracts.target_behavior: Both topologies retain generation and source-order authority while delivery clocks stay non-authoritative.
contracts.migration: Add common coverage fixtures without replacing durable ordering.
contracts.rollback: The durable RFC 011 reconciliation loop remains selectable.

evidence.claim: Durable observation coalesces hints into bounded reconciliation work.
Common coverage comparison tests are driver-ordered and treat generation replacement as incomparable rather than as clock progress.
Scheduler tests coalesce notification hints while serializing the same source object and generation.
Scoped coverage tests advance only at the matching admitted and offered source boundary.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Adapters emit storage-agnostic facts without receiving a database handle.
contracts.target_behavior: Adapters additionally receive no private watcher, cursor, queue, query, or delivery authority.
contracts.migration: Replace remaining private mechanics with declared common source and scope primitives.
contracts.rollback: Legacy adapters stay behind compatibility selection until their declarations pass conformance.

evidence.claim: Architecture checks reject adapter-to-storage and common-to-concrete-adapter edges.
Architecture ratchets reject adapter-owned access authority, storage dependencies, topology-dependent shared decoding, and missing built-in support bindings.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Backfill and live ingestion share decoders and projections.
contracts.target_behavior: Durable and scoped topologies share source-record identity, decoder, facts, provenance, and reducers but use distinct delivery projections.
contracts.migration: Add topology-parity fixtures before enabling the scoped observer.
contracts.rollback: Keep the durable topology and legacy single-file tail until parity and migration gates pass.

evidence.claim: Durable and scoped usage contributions carry SemanticRevisionRef; overlay replacement is grouped by canonical fact identity; observer delivery is deduplicated by event_id; coverage comparison gates overlay retirement.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Durable cursor, fact, projection, and outbox publication is commit-atomic.
contracts.target_behavior: Durable atomicity remains; the non-persistent observer uses explicit bootstrap and epoch barriers instead.
contracts.migration: Keep durable transaction fixtures and add scoped barrier/reset fixtures.
contracts.rollback: Disable the scoped observer without changing durable transactions.

evidence.claim: The durable writer commits source, fact, projection, and change state together.
Scoped composition tests cover reset state, ordered idempotent bootstrap, and atomic whole-epoch source/coverage/reducer replacement.
Scoped delivery invalidates a saturated epoch explicitly and republishes a complete replacement snapshot rather than offering a partial one.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Runtime observation is delivered through durable changes after commit.
contracts.target_behavior: A non-authoritative, database-free observer may deliver the same semantic evidence for one declared session scope.
contracts.migration: Chopsticks moves from watchSessionTranscript to observeSession with one release of overlap (RFC 012 landing plan §7 Wave 3). The feature-flagged TypeScript shadow that preceded this was deleted with the native transport it wrapped: it had no consumer and produced no parity evidence.
contracts.rollback: watchSessionTranscript stays exported from the SDK barrel, and durable observation stays authoritative, until the compatibility window closes.

evidence.claim: §3.1 defines the observeSession surface that replaces the scoped-observation shadow: all 11 event families, deterministic event_id/scope_epoch/SemanticRevisionRef, and overflow to a new epoch with full snapshot replacement.
The legacy tail is the rollback path and is reachable from the SDK barrel for the whole compatibility window.
The store-free observer is reachable from Node and delivers typed revisions for a real session tree; watchSessionTranscript remains the fallback tail until the downstream migration lands.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Adapters may discover sources or reconcile entities through implementation-defined callbacks.
contracts.target_behavior: Only bounded declarations, restricted joins, and common runtime mechanics are conforming.
contracts.migration: Inventory each callback and map it to an approved primitive or an unsupported disposition.
contracts.rollback: Unmigrated adapters remain on an explicitly versioned legacy support release; no new escape hatch is allowed.

evidence.claim: Architecture ratchets reject adapter-private storage, access authority, and missing built-in support bindings including the fourth Factory adapter.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Usage-bearing native rows contribute through the RFC 011 accounting model.
contracts.target_behavior: Canonical usage is a qualified response-level revision keyed primarily by native message identity.
contracts.migration: Build usage-v2 in shadow, compare with an independent response-group oracle, then switch transactionally.
contracts.rollback: Retain legacy usage rows and query selection through the migration window.

evidence.claim: The independent census demonstrates repeated usage rows per response group.
The frozen independent response-level oracle is executable and stable.
Usage-v2 projection tests match the independent qualified oracle, replace response snapshots, and leave legacy usage unchanged.
Query-pack selection tests require ready complete coverage and roll back explicitly even when usage-v2 is pending.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Projection readiness uses generic pack states including StaleSafe.
contracts.target_behavior: Readiness is one vector {catalog, history, usage, capabilities, artifacts, search} derived from committed rows; the catalog field is ready or explicitly degraded long before the others converge.
contracts.migration: Commit discovery rows per source on engine open, then derive every readiness field from them; no durable state machine or publication record is kept.
contracts.rollback: Block startup on full convergence and serve only the history path.

evidence.claim: One readiness vector, derived from committed rows, distinguishes a queryable catalog from complete-only search.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Common message, content, run, and deterministic fact identities feed durable projections.
contracts.target_behavior: Existing facts remain until an explicitly versioned family contract replaces their representation.
contracts.migration: Add versioned revisions in parallel and compare reduced semantic state.
contracts.rollback: Keep legacy fact/projector readers through each family migration window.

evidence.claim: The common fact batch and deterministic legacy fact IDs remain covered by Rust tests.
Versioned interaction serialization is frozen beside usage-v2 actor fixtures.
Versioned model effective-state serialization covers qualified configured, response-observed, and retract identities.
Effort remains an independent qualified configured and response-observed dimension.
Session mode remains independent and requires native-transition evidence before becoming effective.
Permission mode remains independent and requires native-transition evidence before becoming effective.
The message fixture binds a typed content-block correction, complete retraction, and partial non-retraction to one message-scoped canonical block identity.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Source instances and facts have deterministic engine-local identities.
contracts.target_behavior: Persistable external entity and semantic revision references are restart-stable and equal across durable and scoped topologies.
contracts.migration: Introduce versioned canonical references beside legacy runtime-ID-based keys, then migrate each family explicitly.
contracts.rollback: Legacy internal keys remain readable but are never exposed as RFC 012 references.

evidence.claim: Rust derives the v1 references and coverage fixture; the portable TypeScript SDK validates it and agrees on comparison outcomes.
Selected actor-run, affiliation, and usage-v2 identities survive durable rows and scoped envelopes under SemanticRevisionRef.

contracts.legacy_behavior: Query results carry at_commit_seq and use stable keyset pagination.
contracts.target_behavior: Aggregate-facing history/runtime continuations remain on one retained snapshot or fail with explicit expiration.
contracts.migration: Add snapshot identity to the affected cursor contracts and test concurrent commits.
contracts.rollback: Legacy non-aggregate query endpoints remain available during cursor-version migration.

evidence.claim: Existing query conformance covers stable keyset pagination.
Usage-v2 aggregate pages retain one durable watermark and reject a continuation after generation-changing replacement as expired.
Search continuation tests reject cross-scope reuse and expire after the bound durable watermark changes.
Timeline continuation tests remain stable across irrelevant commits and expire when the bound session revision changes.

contracts.legacy_behavior: A durable commit watermark participates in live-update handoff.
contracts.target_behavior: at_commit_seq remains durable-only; semantic references and comparable source/family coverage reconcile scoped evidence.
contracts.migration: Expose common references and coverage on durable pages and observer barriers before enabling merge.
contracts.rollback: Consumers may disable the scoped overlay and read durable state only.

evidence.claim: Durable/live merge deduplicates by event_id, preserves A-B-A, retires complete overlays, and keeps stale overlay on incomparable coverage.
